name: Aztreonam
executiveSummary: Monobactam against Gram-negatives. Adult **1–2 g IV every 8 h** (severe up to **2 g every 6 h**; max **8 g/day**). Pediatrics **30 mg/kg every 6–8 h** (**90–120 mg/kg/day**); CF up to **150 mg/kg/day**.
indications:
## Indications

- Serious aerobic Gram-negative infections in β-lactam allergy / when directed monotherapy is needed.
- Cystic fibrosis (IV; inhaled with specific products).
- No Gram-positive or anaerobic coverage — combine if the focus requires it.

## Precautions

- Renal adjustment. Each gram contains arginine (~780 mg) — consider in liver disease.
- Do not mix in the same line with other drugs if incompatible; prefer flush.

> Low cross-reactivity with penicillins, but not zero in severe allergy.

adulto.dose: Moderate: **1 g IV every 8 h**. Severe / Pseudomonas: **2 g every 6–8 h**. Max **8 g/day**. Adjust by CrCl.
adulto.administration: Reconstitute 10 mL SW; dilute in ~100 mL NS/D5W; infuse **20–60 min**. IM possible in selected doses.
adulto.notes: Do not Y-site with other drugs without checking compatibility.

pediatrico.dose: **30 mg/kg every 6–8 h** (**90–120 mg/kg/day**; max **8 g/day**). Cystic fibrosis: up to **~150 mg/kg/day** divided every 8 h.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted: up to ~7 days refrigerated (label).
- Diluted: check local product insert.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Rash, diarrhea, nausea, phlebitis, ↑ liver enzymes, eosinophilia; rare: neutropenia, *C. difficile*.
